segments: Tenth Dynasty:
The Arab Kings.
Saladin persuaded the woman with promises,
and that he would take one of her daughters for his son.
Then she, when she was won over,
asked that the fortress of Hatakh remain hers.
And she surrendered Mayyafariqin to Saladin,
and she went to Hatakh.
And Qutb al-Din Sukman, son of Nur al-Din, son of Qara Arslan, the lord of Amid, also came to Saladin,
and was received with honor,
and returned to his city.
And Saladin set out from Mayyafariqin and went and encamped on the bank of the river Qaramān (or Qara-mān);
and from there he went to Kafar Zammar (Zimmar,
Zammar?), which is on the Tigris River.
And the people of Mosul, when they were hard pressed by the blockade,
again sent those women to Saladin to plead for peace.
'Imad al-Din, the lord of Shayzar, mediated between them,
and 'Izz al-Din, the lord of Mosul, gave the region of Shahrazur and the whole country east of both Zab rivers, Bayt Waziq and the rest, to Saladin;
and he agreed that Saladin should be proclaimed in Mosul,
and that silver and gold coins should be struck in his name.
And on these terms peace was made.
And Saladin went to Harran,
and he fell ill there with a severe sickness,
and recovered from it.
And while Saladin was ill in Harran,
there was with him his cousin Nasir al-Din, the son of Asad al-Din Shirkuh.
This man, thinking that Saladin would not live,
left him and went to Hims, his city.
And he gathered young men to himself and made them swear to his face
that when Saladin died, he himself would take the kingdom.
But God willed that Saladin recovered,
and that Nasir al-Din died.
And Saladin went to Hims,
and took everything that belonged to him.
And to his son, who was a young boy,
he gave the name Malik Mujahid,
and established him in his father's place.
It is said
that after a year this boy came before Saladin,
and he asked him,
"How far have you recited in the Quran?" And the boy answered,
"As far as the verse:
'Those who devour the possessions of orphans,
it is fire that they devour into their bellies.'"
And Saladin was astonished at his intelligence, and said,
"If he said this knowingly,
one ought to be afraid of him."
